change_summary: PLOS ONE retracted this paper because of concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. The notice says these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, and the author did not respond or could not be reached. The whole paper is retracted and its reported results can't be relied on.
evaluation: Your draft cites Dutta [14] in Section 3 as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM, relying on the reported 97.4% and 96.8% accuracy. In Section 4 you cite Dutta [14] for the LURL model settings you start from, such as two layers and hidden size 650. The notice retracts the paper and says its concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. Both uses are touched: the Section 3 evidence and the Section 4 settings come from the retracted paper. The impact on your draft is high, because the retraction covers the whole paper and your detector choice and starting settings both depend on it.
recommendation: The notice retracts the paper and says its concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, and your draft cites it in Section 3 as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM and in Section 4 for the starting settings. The impact is high because the retracted paper is both your main evidence for the detector choice and the source of your model settings. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor before going further, since the methods depend on the paper and editing the text won't fix it. Replace or remove the Section 3 evidence, re-derive the Section 4 settings, and cite the retraction notice if you mention the paper.
